transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Ms. Anderson, thank you for coming back to see me. I wanted to talk to you about your delivery and some things that happened with your care.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Of course. I have a few minutes before my meeting.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Right. So, we reviewed the charts from your prenatal visits and the delivery records. It looks like there was a failure in the communication chain. You were GBS positive, meaning you had Group B streptococcus in your records, but that information wasn't relayed to the labour and delivery team. Because of that, the prophylactic antibiotics weren't administered during the birth.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I see.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm sorry that this confusion happened. We were very busy on the unit that night and it seems the handoff just didn't happen correctly.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I understand.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It's a bit of a systemic breakdown in how the data is transferred.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is the baby okay?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The baby is currently being monitored and is stable, but we need to be vigilant.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That's a relief.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Was it a mistake by the nurse or the doctor?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It's really just a failure in the documentation flow across the different departments.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I see.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I just want to make sure we are on the same page.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I think I understand.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I actually have to get to a rounding group in a few minutes, so I want to make sure we cover the next steps quickly.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That is fine.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We have started the baby on a course of antibiotics now as a precaution. We will keep the baby in the neonatal unit for another forty-eight hours for observation.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And what do I need to do?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You just need to keep alerting the nursing staff if you notice any changes in the baby's temperature or feeding patterns. I will personally check the labs tomorrow morning at eight and I'll come by your room at ten to give you the update.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Thank you.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You're welcome.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Will this be noted in the permanent record?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes, the incident is being documented in the system.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I appreciate the honesty.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Will there be a follow-up appointment specifically for this?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The pediatrician will handle that during the standard discharge visit on Thursday.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Alright.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll let you get back to your day then.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Thank you, doctor.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language, stating they have to get to a rounding group and want to cover next steps 'quickly'.

E.justification: Error (failure to give GBS antibiotics) named in the second turn, lay language used, and comprehension checked twice ('make sure we are on the same page', 'I think I understand').

A.justification: While the resident says 'I'm sorry', they deflect responsibility to the 'communication chain', 'systemic breakdown', and 'documentation flow' when asked who made the mistake.

R.justification: Resident uses generic validation ('I understand') twice without naming specific emotions or engaging deeply with the patient's emotional state.

T.justification: Plan includes specific steps (antibiotics, 48h observation), timelines (tomorrow at 8am/10am, Thursday discharge), patient role (alerting staff to temp/feeding), and prevention (incident documented in system).
